results.evidence: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) is a method that helps an LLM use fresh or private information. The name has three words. Retrieval means finding and fetching relevant pieces of information from an outside source. Augmented means added to or made stronger. We add the retrieved text to the question in the prompt. Generation means the LLM writes the answer using the question plus the retrieved context.

results.evidence: One limitation: the answer is only as good as the retrieved chunks (small pieces of a document). If the search returns wrong or outdated chunks, the answer can be wrong. The LLM can still hallucinate or ignore the context.

results.evidence: RAG lets the LLM use up-to-date and private information. You just add new documents to the knowledge base. RAG reduces made-up answers (hallucinations), though it does not remove them completely. Answers can show their sources, so you can check them. RAG is cheaper and faster than retraining (teaching the model again from scratch) or fine-tuning (training the model further on new examples, which changes its weights). Fine-tuning is slower, costlier, and mainly used to change style or behaviour. Knowledge is easy to update by changing the documents, not the model.
